910.name: Prehistoric Sweden & Vendel Era
910.description: Sweden's prehistory from post-glacial settlement through the Nordic Bronze Age, the Iron Age, and the splendid Vendel Era with its warrior aristocracy and richly decorated helmets — the immediate precursor to the Viking Age.

sub_clusters.name: Bronze Age & Rock Carvings
sub_clusters.description: Post-glacial settlement, the Nordic Bronze Age with its elaborate solar symbolism, the Tanum rock carvings (UNESCO), the Kivik tomb, and extensive maritime trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Vendel Era & Old Uppsala
sub_clusters.description: The Swedish Iron Age, the Vendel Period (550–793) with its magnificent warrior aristocracy, the royal mounds at Old Uppsala (Gamla Uppsala), the Svear and Götar tribal kingdoms, and the proto-state formation.

920.name: Swedish Viking Age & Varangians
920.description: Swedish Vikings (Varangians) pioneered the eastern route — through Russia to Constantinople and Baghdad — founding the Rus' state, serving as the Byzantine Emperor's elite Varangian Guard, and establishing vast trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Varangians & the Foundation of Rus'
sub_clusters.description: Swedish Vikings sailing east via the river systems of Russia, the semi-legendary Rurik's founding of the Rus' state at Novgorod (862), and the establishment of the trade route 'from the Varangians to the Greeks' linking Scandinavia to Byzantium.
key_events: Varangian Rus' establish trading settlements along the rivers from the Baltic to the Black Sea and Constantinople (9th century)

sub_clusters.name: Birka & Christianisation of Sweden
sub_clusters.description: The trading town of Birka on Lake Mälaren, Ansgar's mission (829), the gradual Christianisation of Sweden — the last Scandinavian country to convert — the destruction of the pagan temple at Uppsala, and the rise of Sigtuna.

920.name: Medieval Sweden & Kalmar Union
920.description: The consolidation of the medieval Swedish kingdom, the Northern Crusades in Finland, the Hanseatic influence, and Sweden's turbulent membership in the Kalmar Union, culminating in the Stockholm Bloodbath and Gustav Vasa's rebellion.

sub_clusters.name: Folkunga Dynasty & Finnish Crusades
sub_clusters.description: The Folkunga dynasty, Birger Jarl's consolidation of royal power, the Swedish crusades to Finland, Magnus Eriksson's national law code, the Black Death's impact, and the political crises leading to the Kalmar Union.

sub_clusters.name: Kalmar Union & Stockholm Bloodbath
sub_clusters.description: Sweden's resistance to Danish dominance within the Kalmar Union, Engelbrekt's rebellion (1434), the Sture regents, and Christian II's Stockholm Bloodbath (1520) — the massacre of Swedish nobles that provoked Gustav Vasa's liberation war.
key_events: Stockholm Bloodbath — Christian II executes over 80 Swedish nobles (1520)

930.name: Vasa Dynasty & Great Power Era
930.description: Gustav Vasa's liberation of Sweden and the Reformation, followed by Sweden's rise to European great power status under Gustavus Adolphus, the Baltic empire, and Charles XII's dramatic fall — encompassing the entire Stormaktstiden.

sub_clusters.name: Gustav Vasa & Nation-Building
sub_clusters.description: Gustav Vasa's election as king (6 June 1523 — Sweden's National Day), the break with the Catholic Church, the Swedish Reformation, the confiscation of church properties, the centralisation of administration, and the establishment of hereditary monarchy.
key_events: Gustav Vasa elected King of Sweden, breaking from the Kalmar Union (6 June 1523)

sub_clusters.name: Vasa Sons & Succession Crises
sub_clusters.description: The turbulent reigns of Gustav Vasa's sons — Erik XIV's madness and deposition, John III's Counter-Reformation tendencies, Sigismund's Catholicism and the loss of the Polish-Swedish union — and Duke Charles (IX)'s Protestant coup.

sub_clusters.name: Gustavus Adolphus & the Thirty Years' War
sub_clusters.description: Gustavus Adolphus's military revolution, the Swedish intervention in the Thirty Years' War (1630), the victory at Breitenfeld (1631), Gustavus's death at Lützen (1632), and the Peace of Westphalia granting Sweden territories in northern Germany.
key_events: Gustavus Adolphus killed at the Battle of Lützen after turning the tide of the Thirty Years' War (1632)

sub_clusters.name: Charles XII & the Great Northern War
sub_clusters.description: Charles XII's brilliant early victories at Narva (1700), the fateful invasion of Russia, the catastrophic defeat at Poltava (1709), exile in the Ottoman Empire, and his death at Fredriksten (1718) ending Swedish great-power status.

940.name: Age of Liberty to Bernadotte Dynasty
940.description: The post-Great-Power recovery: the Age of Liberty's parliamentary experiments, Linnaeus, Gustav III's enlightened absolutism and assassination, the loss of Finland, the Bernadotte dynasty, the Norwegian union and dissolution, and mass emigration to America.

sub_clusters.name: Age of Liberty & Linnaeus
sub_clusters.description: The Age of Liberty (Frihetstiden) with its parliamentary government, the Hats and Caps party struggle, Carl Linnaeus's revolutionary biological taxonomy, and the flowering of Swedish Enlightenment culture.

sub_clusters.name: Gustavian Era & Royal Assassination
sub_clusters.description: Gustav III's coup restoring royal power (1772), his patronage of arts and culture (founding the Swedish Academy, the Royal Opera), his assassination at a masked ball (1792), and the disastrous loss of Finland to Russia (1809).

sub_clusters.name: Bernadotte Dynasty & Union with Norway
sub_clusters.description: Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte (Charles XIV John) elected crown prince, the union with Norway (1814), Oscar II and the industrialisation of Sweden, the mass emigration to North America (over 1 million Swedes), and the peaceful dissolution of the Norwegian union (1905).

sub_clusters.name: Industrialisation & Social Movements
sub_clusters.description: Sweden's rapid industrialisation, Alfred Nobel's inventions and legacy, the labour movement, universal male suffrage demands, the founding of the Social Democratic Party (1889), and the pre-WWI neutrality position.

950.name: WWI Neutrality & Democratic Breakthrough
950.description: Swedish neutrality in WWI, the democratic breakthrough with universal suffrage (1919–1921), the Social Democrats' rise to dominance, and the Saltsjöbaden Agreement establishing the 'Swedish model' of labour relations.

sub_clusters.name: Neutrality & Universal Suffrage
sub_clusters.description: Swedish neutrality during WWI, food shortages and the hunger demonstrations of 1917, the granting of universal suffrage (men 1909/women 1919, fully effective 1921), and the transition to parliamentary democracy.

sub_clusters.name: Social Democratic Hegemony Begins
sub_clusters.description: Per Albin Hansson's vision of Sweden as the 'People's Home' (Folkhemmet), the Saltsjöbaden Agreement (1938) between employers and unions, and the foundations of the Swedish welfare state.

950.name: WWII Swedish Neutrality
950.description: Sweden's contested neutrality during WWII — permitting German troops to transit to Norway, trading iron ore with Germany, but also sheltering refugees including nearly all of Denmark's Jews and Raoul Wallenberg's rescue of Hungarian Jews.

sub_clusters.name: Wartime Neutrality & Compromises
sub_clusters.description: Sweden's armed neutrality, the controversial iron ore exports and transit permissions, the midsummer crisis of 1941, and the moral dilemmas of neutrality between Nazi Germany and the Allies.

sub_clusters.name: Raoul Wallenberg & Refugee Rescue
sub_clusters.description: Sweden's sheltering of Danish Jews (1943), Count Folke Bernadotte's White Buses rescue operation, and Raoul Wallenberg's heroic rescue of tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews in Budapest (1944–1945) before his disappearance into Soviet captivity.
key_events: Raoul Wallenberg saves tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews in Budapest through protective passports (1944–1945)

960.name: Swedish Welfare State & Folkhemmet
960.description: The zenith of the Swedish welfare state model: social democratic governance, the 'Swedish model' of labour relations, Olof Palme's international activism, the assassination shock (1986), and the economic crisis of the early 1990s.

sub_clusters.name: Welfare State Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The Social Democrats' unbroken 44 years in power (1932–1976), the construction of the comprehensive welfare state, the 'Million Programme' housing, ABBA and Swedish cultural export, and the co-determination reforms.

sub_clusters.name: Palme Era & Assassination
sub_clusters.description: Olof Palme's activist foreign policy (Vietnam, apartheid, nuclear disarmament), his assassination on a Stockholm street (28 February 1986) — Sweden's 'loss of innocence' — the unsolved case finally closed in 2020, and the banking crisis of 1991–1992.
key_events: Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme assassinated on a Stockholm street (28 February 1986)

960.name: Contemporary Sweden
960.description: Post-Cold War Sweden: EU membership (1995), the tech boom (Spotify, IKEA), the 2015 migration crisis, the end of non-alignment, and NATO membership (2024).

sub_clusters.name: EU Membership & Tech Innovation
sub_clusters.description: EU accession (1995), rejection of the euro (2003), Sweden's emergence as a tech and startup hub (Spotify, Skype, Klarna, King), the assassination of Foreign Minister Anna Lindh (2003), and Swedish cultural influence.

sub_clusters.name: Migration Crisis & Political Shift
sub_clusters.description: The 2015 refugee crisis (163,000 asylum seekers), the rise of the Sweden Democrats, the rightward shift in immigration policy, gang violence debates, and the transformation of the Swedish political landscape.

sub_clusters.name: NATO Membership & Security Transformation
sub_clusters.description: Russia's invasion of Ukraine prompting Sweden's historic NATO application (2022), the Turkish and Hungarian ratification delays, and Sweden's accession as NATO's 32nd member (7 March 2024), ending over 200 years of military non-alignment.
key_events: Sweden joins NATO as the 32nd member state, ending over 200 years of non-alignment (7 March 2024)

sub_clusters.name: Swedish Cultural & Global Influence
sub_clusters.description: Sweden's outsized global cultural impact through music (ABBA, Avicii, Max Martin), design (IKEA, H&M), gaming (Minecraft, Paradox), the Nobel Prizes, and the Greta Thunberg climate movement.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
